correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the single random u gives independent N(0,S) probes, where S=||Mᵀu||²=Σs_i²G_i²>0 almost surely. The standardized probes have a law independent of u, so the squared denominator is SW with independent W~χ²_ℓ. Integrating the smooth anisotropic Gaussian density over the radius-√x ball gives F_S(x)=a_S x^{r/2}(1+O(x)), with a_S=1/[2^{r/2}Γ(1+r/2)∏s_i]; the radial density gives the matching relative error. The χ² coefficient a_W is the same without ∏s_i and with ℓ in place of r. Conditioning on the factor with the larger exponent gives dominated convergence via its finite negative moment. At equality, splitting at x/ε and ε leaves two O(x^{r/2}) ends and a middle integral (r/2)a_S a_W x^{r/2}∫dy/y with O(x^{r/2}) error. Substituting x=ℓF²/τ² gives the factor two in front of log τ and the stated constants, including the gamma negative moment and the Laplace integral by Tonelli. Integrating the tail proves the sharp inverse-moment cutoff, with divergence also at equality. Conditional SLLN proves the limit F/√S (Var(S)=2Σs_i⁴>0). These are fixed nonzero spectra, not a uniform varying-rank claim. Frozen verification notes and supplied checker were inspected but not executed. Independent isotropic quadrature integrating the product CDF gave exact/leading ratios 0.9996264, 0.9860243, 0.9934920 and 0.9934920 at (r,ℓ,τ)=(1,3,80),(2,2,250),(2,3,250),(3,2,250).

value.rationale: Reusing a random left probe is a natural reduction in sampling/storage that leaves all right draws conditionally independent. The theorem gives a precise reliability cost: a rank-controlled failure exponent, a calibrated logarithmic penalty exactly at matching rank and probe count, and a nonvanishing random error even with unlimited right draws. Both the inverse-moment frontier and anisotropic leading constants can be needed when using such probes for norm validation.
